findings.title: traceID and plugin/datasource fields dropped from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log
findings.body: The refactor removes pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID from the completed-request log params and relies entirely on the context logger. ContextualLoggerMiddleware (contextual_logger_middleware.go) only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname; it never adds traceID. The traceID field that the old code attached via tracing.TraceIDFromContext is therefore lost from this log line, which breaks correlation of plugin egress logs with traces for anyone querying on traceID. Either add traceID to the contextual attributes or keep it in logRequest.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware being placed earlier in the chain
findings.body: Fields that were previously explicit in logRequest now only appear if the context carries them, which only happens when ContextualLoggerMiddleware runs before LoggerMiddleware. In CreateMiddlewares this ordering is implicit and undocumented, and the removed doc comment on MetricsMiddleware ('this middleware should live at the top of the middleware stack') gave no replacement. Reordering the list, or using LoggerMiddleware without the contextual middleware, will silently drop all identifying fields from the log with no error or test failure.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no tests
findings.body: The attributes that were previously covered by the instrumentation path (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) are now produced by this new middleware, but there is no test verifying that the contextual logger is attached to the context or that the attributes are correct. The existing metrics test was only renamed and does not exercise any logging context. Similarly, the changed LoggerMiddleware output has no test.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext ignores the context and returns a fresh logger
findings.body: FromContext discards its context and returns a new TestLogger, so the logs recorded by tests are not connected to the logger returned for a given context. Any test that wants to assert that LoggerMiddleware logs via a context-derived logger will see its calls on a different instance than the one it inspects, making such assertions impossible or misleading.

findings.title: FromContext silently discards the context when the type assertion fails
findings.body: If the underlying infra logger's FromContext does not return a *log.ConcreteLogger, the wrapper falls back to d.New() which carries none of the context attributes. This is a silent loss of all contextual fields with no log or error, and it is not covered by any test.

findings.title: Logger name 'plugin.instrumentation' is stale after the rename
findings.body: The middleware is now named MetricsMiddleware and the logging concern lives in LoggerMiddleware, yet the logger is still named 'plugin.instrumentation'. This keeps the old 'instrumentation' terminology the PR aims to remove and makes the log source inconsistent with the new naming.

findings.title: Test function still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after rename
findings.body: The file and constructor were renamed to MetricsMiddleware, but the test function keeps the old TestInstrumentationMiddleware name, leaving the rename incomplete and making it harder to find the test for the renamed type.
